$$h\in H_J\cap\tau,\qquad T_J\cap\tau\ne\varnothing,$$
then the unique endpoint neighbour of  $h$  in  $T_J$  belongs to  $\tau$ .Suppose instead that this neighbour lies outside  $\tau$ . Then  $h$  cannot be adjacent to any endpoint of  $J$  inside  $\tau$ , so the only possible such endpoint is the corner diagonally opposite  $h$ . Call it  $x$ .Only two neighbours of  $x$  lie outside its tile. Its intrinsic degree three therefore requires an occupied neighbour inside the tile. That neighbour must be another support, adjacent both to  $x$  and to  $h$ , contradicting support degree one. ∎Lemma 2: each original meets a tile in a connected endpoint setEvery nonempty  $T_J\cap\tau$  induces a connected graph.The only disconnected possibility is two diagonal endpoints. Exact cancellation of the source-labelled eventsWe first work with an arbitrary endpoint-disjoint inventory  $K$ , which need not be complete.For a physical tile  $\tau$ , define: $n_\tau$ : the number of endpoints in  $\tau$ ; $e_\tau$ : the number of unordered intratile edges between endpoints; $k_\tau$ : the number of originals having endpoints in  $\tau$ ; $h_\tau$ : the number of original support incidences in  $\tau$ , counted once for each original whose endpoint set meets  $\tau$ ; $r_\tau$ : the part of  $h_\tau$  not consumed by the endpoint union; $c_\tau$ : the indicator that  $\tau$  is full and owned by one original; $f_\tau$ : the indicator that  $\tau$  is full mixed.Both  $h_\tau$  and  $r_\tau$  retain owner multiplicities. This is essential at the incomplete old inventory, where two originals can name the same unconsumed support.By Lemma 2, the total number of intratile endpoint edges belonging to individual originals is
$$n_\tau-k_\tau+c_\tau.$$
Consequently the number of cross-owner endpoint edges is
$$e_\tau-(n_\tau-k_\tau+c_\tau).$$
Each such edge initially supplies two directed, source-labelled contacts. By Lemma 1, every consumed support counted in  $h_\tau-r_\tau$  corresponds to exactly one of the contacts excluded by the immutable original support rule. Therefore the event count is exactly
$$E_\tau
=
2\bigl(e_\tau-(n_\tau-k_\tau+c_\tau)\bigr)
-(h_\tau-r_\tau).                                             \tag{2}$$
This is where retaining support exclusions after consumption matters: the consumed-support incidence still removes its directed contact from  $E_\tau$ .The tile contribution to  $-\sum q_J$  is
$$2k_\tau-\frac12n_\tau-h_\tau.$$
Substituting (2), and using  $c_\tau+f_\tau=\mathbf1[n_\tau=4]$ , gives
$$\begin{aligned}
&2k_\tau-\frac12n_\tau-h_\tau+2f_\tau-E_\tau\\
&\qquad=\frac32n_\tau-2e_\tau-r_\tau+2\mathbf1[n_\tau=4].
\end{aligned}$$
Define
$$\beta_\tau(K)
=
\frac32n_\tau-2e_\tau-r_\tau+2\mathbf1[n_\tau=4].$$
We have proved the exact identity
$$\boxed{\displaystyle
\Phi(K)=2P(K)+\sum_\tau\beta_\tau(K).
}                                                               \tag{3}$$
It holds before completeness, with the original-support multiplicities specified above. It follows from the immutable charges and the source-labelled event definition; it does not replace either of them by a different inventory.4. Hence
$$\beta_\tau=2-\frac12n_\tau-r_\tau.                              \tag{4}$$

With three endpoints, the missing corner is adjacent to two endpoints and cannot be a retained support.Thus the only negative tile is a singleton endpoint together with its two retained supports. 5.2 Every negative rotor tile forces a distinct positive tileOnly the rotor’s two-L phases can have negative singleton tiles. By the tile-preserving symmetries already described, it suffices to use shape  $A$  translated by  $(1,0)$ . Its endpoints are

Associate it with the tile

That tile contains three endpoints of this rotor and is missing  $(2,0)$ .If the singleton tile is negative,  $(1,0)$  remains a support. An endpoint at  $(2,0)$ , of any owner, would give this support two occupied neighbours:
$$(1,1)\quad\text{and}\quad(2,0).$$
Completeness forbids that. The associated tile therefore remains a three-endpoint tile and contributes  $+1/2$ .Likewise, the lower singleton  $(4,2)$  has supports

$$[2,3]\times[2,3],$$
whose missing corner is  $(3,3)$ . The retained support  $(4,3)$  forbids an endpoint at that corner, so this tile also remains a  $+1/2$  triple tile.The association is injective:The two mate tiles within one rotor are distinct.A mate tile contains three endpoints of its rotor. Two different rotors cannot each own three endpoints in a four-site tile.Thus every negative rotor tile has an explicitly identified, distinct positive mate. There is no assumed Hall allocation.6. $$\Delta(C\mid O)=1+6-4=3.$$

$$\boxed{\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}\ge0}$$
holds, with the stronger uniform lower bound above. The prescribed whole-family identity remains
$$\Phi(\mathrm{full})
=-g+\sum_i\Delta_i+\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}.$$
The cap value  $5$  is compatible with the new accounting. In the supplied long-wall cap construction,  $P_{\mathrm{out}}=1$ , its terminal tiles are filled, and the two surviving outer-wall tip tiles contribute  $1/2$  each. Equation (11) gives
$$2+2+1=5.$$
I have not established that  $5$  is the sharp universal minimum, nor found a complete counterexample below it. Formula (12) nevertheless restricts any such counterexample:It must have  $P_{\mathrm{out}}\le2$ .If  $P_{\mathrm{out}}=2$ , integrality forces any value below  $5$  to be  $4$ . $$N_{\mathrm U}=4,\qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=0.$$
Both positive-charge exterior U sources would have to retain both negative terminal tiles, and every remaining unpaired exterior tile weight would have to vanish.Those residual patterns are not asserted to be extendible. The resolved result is the unrestricted exterior sign, proved from the complete retained-support condition and the supplied canonical records, without a dimension cutoff, a cap assumption, or an arbitrary-grid decomposition claim.
